questionText: Which one of the following statements is TRUE with respect to levelling survey?

options.html: A level surface at all points is normal to the direction of the force of gravity.
options.text: A level surface at all points is normal to the direction of the force of gravity.

options.html: Two level surfaces can cross each other.
options.text: Two level surfaces can cross each other.

options.html: Ellipsoid is an irregular surface approximating the physical surface of the Earth.
options.text: Ellipsoid is an irregular surface approximating the physical surface of the Earth.

options.html: Geoid is a regular surface approximating the physical surface of the Earth.
options.text: Geoid is a regular surface approximating the physical surface of the Earth.

explanationHtml:
(A) TRUE: A level surface is an equipotential surface of gravity - by definition, the force of gravity (plumb line) is perpendicular (normal) to a level surface at every point.

(B) FALSE: Two level surfaces can never cross each other - they are equipotential surfaces of the Earth's gravity field. If they crossed, a point would have two different potential values, which is impossible.

(C) FALSE: The Geoid (not Ellipsoid) is the irregular surface approximating the physical surface. The Ellipsoid is a smooth mathematical surface.

(D) FALSE: The Geoid is actually an irregular surface (it follows mean sea level including undulations). The Ellipsoid is the regular mathematical surface.

explanationHtml:

Concept:
HPC=RL of P+BS\text{HPC} = \text{RL of P} + \text{BS}HPC=RL of P+BS

Therefore:
RL of P=HPC−BS\text{RL of P} = \text{HPC} - \text{BS}RL of P=HPC−BS

Explanation: The staff reading (back sight) is taken at a known/benchmark point. The HPC is height of the instrument line of sight. The RL of P is obtained by subtracting the staff reading from the HPC.
